title: Retriage queue against objectives
goal: The user reordered what matters in the objectives, so the task queue has to be checked against it. Every open task should sit at a priority and in an order that matches what the objectives now say comes first, with no duplicates, and each task should say in plain words which objective it serves.
notes: The user updated queue/objectives.json and asked for a retriage. Read the objectives tree (order is priority, nesting is sub-epics) and every open task, then make the queue reflect it: reprioritize (queue.mjs priority), resequence to clean steps of 10 per priority (queue.mjs seq), dedupe, and groom notes so each task names the objective it serves. Do NOT write a digest. Record one history event: queue.mjs event triage with a summary of what moved.
acceptance: Every open task priority and sequence is consistent with the objectives ordering, and any task that no longer fits is reclassified, deprioritised or dropped with a reason
Each open task names, in its notes, the objective it serves and why it earns its place
Sequence numbers are clean steps of ten within each priority, and there are no duplicate open tasks
One triage history event summarises what moved, and no digest is written

Adversarial read of the queue, not just a sort. Three things were actually wrong. (1) The built-in components task is specified as drawn from named styles, but the styles task sat at p2 below it, so it would have been claimed before its own prerequisite; styles promoted to p1 and sequenced first, and named as a dep. This reverses steps 7 and 8 of the plan doc on purpose and the reason is written into the task. (2) Two tasks were filed under the epic that found them rather than the one they serve: a playtest harness bug sat under measure-redline and an app Capture menu bug sat under unmanned-loop; swapped. (3) The spec task asked for a page that had since been written under a different name, so it was retargeted to the three things that page genuinely does not say (child coordinate rule, menu items and shortcuts per step, flag names) instead of producing a second source of truth.

Nothing was reprioritised downward and nothing dropped. The 17:01 manager pass had already filed against the same objectives edit (16:48 local is 23:48Z), so the priorities were sound; saying so is the honest result rather than manufacturing churn.
